blocks.content: 1. MEANING AND SCOPE OF EXTERNAL SECTOR

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Balance of Payments (BoP) is a comprehensive record of all economic transactions between residents of India and the rest of the world during a given period.
The Current Account deals with trade in goods (visibles), trade in services (invisibles), primary income, and secondary transfers.
The Capital Account records foreign financial investment flows including Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI), External Commercial Borrowings (ECB), and NRI deposits.
India maintains a managed floating exchange rate system where market forces determine currency values while the RBI intervenes to minimize excessive volatility.
India's Foreign Exchange Reserves consist of Foreign Currency Assets (FCA), Gold holdings, Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), and the Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) in the IMF.

blocks.content: The External Sector refers to all economic transactions between residents of India and the rest of the world. It includes trade in goods and services, capital flows, foreign exchange reserves, exchange rate management and external debt.
The performance of the external sector determines currency stability, trade balance, foreign investment inflows and overall macroeconomic stability.
2. BALANCE OF PAYMENTS (BoP)
Balance of Payments is a systematic record of all economic transactions between India and the rest of the world during a specific period.
BoP must always balance (Credits = Debits).
3. CURRENT ACCOUNT
The Current Account records trade in goods and services, income flows and unilateral transfers.

Trade Balance = Exports – Imports (Goods only).

Current Account Balance = Trade Balance + Net Services + Net Income + Net Transfers.
Current Account Deficit (CAD) occurs when imports exceed exports.
4. CAPITAL & FINANCIAL ACCOUNT
This account records capital flows such as foreign investments and borrowings.

• Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) – Long-term investment with management control.

• Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) – Investment in shares/bonds.

• External Commercial Borrowings (ECB).
5. EXCHANGE RATE SYSTEM IN INDIA
Exchange Rate is the price of one currency in terms of another.
India follows a Managed Floating Exchange Rate system where market forces determine the rate, but RBI intervenes to reduce excessive volatility.
6. EXCHANGE RATE DETERMINATION (DEMAND–SUPPLY THEORY)
Under flexible system, exchange rate is determined by demand and supply of foreign exchange.
Demand for foreign exchange arises from imports, foreign travel, interest payments, and capital outflows.
Supply arises from exports, remittances, FDI, FPI and foreign borrowings.
Equilibrium rate is determined at intersection of demand and supply curves.
7. RUPEE DEPRECIATION vs APPRECIATION

rows: Decrease in the value of the Rupee relative to foreign currencies
Increase in the value of the Rupee relative to foreign currencies
Exports become cheaper and more competitive globally
Exports become more expensive and less competitive
Imports become costlier, expanding the import bill
Imports become cheaper, reducing domestic cost pressure
Increases repayment burden in terms of Indian Rupee
Decreases repayment burden in terms of Indian Rupee

blocks.content: 8. FOREIGN EXCHANGE RESERVES
Forex reserves are assets held by RBI in foreign currencies.

Components:

• Foreign Currency Assets (FCA)

• Gold

• Special Drawing Rights (SDR)

• Reserve Tranche Position (IMF)
High reserves ensure currency stability and protect against external shocks.
9. EXTERNAL DEBT
External debt refers to borrowings from foreign sources.

Indicators:

• External Debt to GDP Ratio

• Short-term debt ratio

• Debt service ratio
10. INDIA’S TRADE COMPOSITION
Major Export Items:

• Petroleum products

• Engineering goods

• Gems & Jewellery

• Pharmaceuticals

• IT services

items: India achieved full convertibility on the Current Account in 1994, but maintains partial convertibility on the Capital Account.
Forex Reserves composition (FCA, Gold, SDR, RTP) is a recurring question in prelims and competitive exams.
Distinguish clearly between Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) long-term stability and Foreign Portfolio Investment (FPI) volatile 'hot money' nature.
Rupee depreciation makes exports cheaper and imports costlier, directly widening the Current Account Deficit when oil import prices surge.

blocks.content: Major Import Items:

• Crude oil

• Gold

• Electronics

• Machinery
11. MAJOR TRADE PARTNERS OF INDIA

Major Export Destinations: USA, UAE, European Union, Bangladesh, Singapore.

Major Import Sources: China, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq.
12. WTO & TRADE POLICY
India is a member of the World Trade Organization (WTO).
Trade policy instruments include tariffs, quotas, export promotion schemes and Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).
